source_title: Everything Jennifer Lawrence Has Revealed About Her Plastic Surgery and Cosmetic Procedures - People.com
source_excerpt:
Jennifer Lawrence has been open about some of the beauty procedures she’s had done over the years, from a breast lift to ‘baby Botox’
Christopher Polk/2026GG/Penske Media via Getty
Jennifer Lawrence has spoken candidly about her cosmetic procedures over the years
The mother of two opened up about her body changing after welcoming her two children
While the actress has revealed she’s gotten a breast lift, she also admitted hesitancy over other procedures
Jennifer Lawrence has been open about the cosmetic procedures she’s undergone.
The Hunger Games actress previously explained how motherhood affected her body after welcoming her two sons, Cy and another young son , whom she shares with her husband, Cooke Maroney .
“Everything bounced back, pretty much, after the first one,” Lawrence told The New Yorker in a profile published in October 2025. “Second one, nothing bounced back.”
Since then, Lawrence revealed that she underwent a breast lift after welcoming her second child in 2025 and has also shared some of the minimally-invasive cosmetic touches she’s had done over the years, including small amounts of Botox. However, she’s also said there are some procedures that she wouldn’t consider.
Here’s everything to know about what Jennifer Lawrence has said about her plastic surgery operations over the years.
Lawrence shared she had a breast lift after welcoming her second son
The Mes founder initially spoke about her plans to get a breast lift in an October 2025 interview with The New Yorker , where she revealed she was undergoing the procedure the following month.
At the time, Lawrence spoke about how motherhood had affected her body while reflecting on filming a nude scene for her 2023 comedy No Hard Feelings . She also said she was expected to appear nude while filming the upcoming drama What Happens at Night roughly one year after giving birth to her second son.
When asked if she would have thought about getting plastic surgery if she wasn’t in the acting industry, Lawrence acknowledged the role her profession played.
“Maybe I wouldn’t be hustling to the appointment in the same way,” she said. “But I think yes.”
In an interview with The Cut published the following year in October 2026, Lawrence confirmed that she underwent a breast lift after welcoming her second child. She explained that, at the time, her body changed differently after the second pregnancy compared to the first.
“I want to be a sexy mom,” she told the publication, sharing her personal ethos on trying to look good with minimal effort. “At drop-off, I want to look like a woman that has her shit together even when I’ve just woken up and don’t have my shit together.”
She confirmed she occasionally gets “baby Botox”
While Lawrence reflected on her decision to get a breast lift in relation to her career, she also said that some aspects of her profession have prevented her from considering other procedures.
The Die My Love actress explained to Vogue in a September 2026 interview that she gets small amounts of Botox — a minimally invasive cosmetic procedure that causes muscles to relax — but otherwise opts to preserve her natural facial expressions.
“Yeah, because I can’t really get very much done. I need to have movement in my face — I get baby Botox, but I can’t do a lot,” she told the publication. “If my skin is going to be a little saggier than I would like, at least it looks dewy and pretty.”
Another minimally invasive procedure that Lawrence avoids is getting dermal fillers, a gel-like substance injected under the skin to appear more voluminous and smooth out wrinkles or enhance facial contours.
Lawrence told The New Yorker that she avoids fillers because they can be too noticeable on camera, and she needs to retain movement in her face and forehead to portray characters who likely wouldn’t have the same access to cosmetic dermatology.
Lawrence teased she is open to the idea of a facelift
While Lawrence hasn’t gotten a facelift, she teased that she’s open to the invasive procedure, which lifts and tightens the deeper facial tissue of the face and neck and trims excess fat and skin.
When asked whether she had already gotten a facelift in The New Yorker profile, Lawrence joked about the possibility of having one in the future.
“No,” she said. “But, believe me, I’m gonna!”
She said she is “nervous” about fat transfers, but is interested in a buccal fat removal
Although Lawrence is open to some treatments, she’s also hesitant about others. One procedure she specifically mentioned that makes her nervous are “fat transfers,” which are invasive procedures that take a patient’s own fat and move it to another part of their body.
“Oh, I’m really nervous about these fat transfers. I support other people doing them because I want to continue to watch and see what happens, but I don’t know about that,” she told Vogue .
However, Lawrence quipped she is more interested in the idea of buccal fat removal , a popular procedure that removes part of the buccal fat pads in the lower cheeks and jawline to make the face look slimmer and more defined.
“I mean, I would love to have a buccal fat removal,” she told Vogue. “I can’t because everybody would know, but just know that I want that.”
Lawrence enjoys skin treatments with radiofrequency
In addition to her non-invasive procedures, Lawrence also utilizes various cosmetic treatments to enhance her skin. The Silver Linings Playbook actress told Vogue that she undergoes Dior’s signature Mascarade treatment , the luxurious, technology-driven facial treatment exclusively available at the Dior Spa Hotel Cipriani in Venice, Italy.
The treatment combines manual facial massages with cutting-edge skincare devices — including ultrasound waves, radiofrequency and microcurrent stimulation — to lift, restore and sculpt the face. In particular, Lawrence said she enjoys the radiofrequency aspect.
“I do like the radiofrequency because I have huge cheeks and so I feel like exercising them as much as possible,” she told Vogue .
However, Lawrence also remembered being initially frightened when the dermatologist misted oxygen over her face during the treatment.
“I thought she was smoking in my face, ” Lawrence recalled. “When you’re in Europe, you never know. But I just felt, like, this poof . But it turned out to not be a cigarette and it was really, really hydrating and refreshing.”
She uses prescription retinoid tretinoin and applies diaper cream on her face
When she isn’t using various procedures to enhance her skin, Lawrence is maximizing preventative care with various skincare treatments and medications.
The American Hustle actress told Vogue that she had recently started a “retinol journey” and has been taking Tretinoin, a prescription-strength topical retinoid that clears acne, fades fine lines and wrinkles and stimulates collagen production.
In order to preserve her skin during the more intense retinoid treatment, Lawrence revealed that she also puts on Desitin, an over-the-counter skin protectant primarily used to prevent diaper rash in babies.
“I fell for that Desitin, the diaper cream at night, which I do stand by — not permanently because it’s not moisturizing,” she told Vogue . “But when you’re going up on retinol and your face gets red, sleeping in the Desitin, I noticed that it did make my pores smaller and it healed the redness.”
She continued, “Well, you have to sandwich . You have to use night cream, like something really moisturizing. Then Tret. Then a spritz of water and oil, because what I didn’t realize for so long, and I’m really happy to tell you this: Oil traps the water in, so you have to give oil some water that the oil sits on top of so that it seals it into your skin.”
In addition to her nighttime routine, Lawrence makes sure to apply sunscreen on her face and her hands to protect her retinol journey.
“I’ve been wearing a scarf over my melasma spots ever since I started Tret, which of course I get photographed and people think I’m making some sort of fashion statement. I’m literally just haggard and scaling and trying to survive,” she joked.
“There’s no amount of looking goofy that I’m going to care about more than my melasma,” she added.
